standard_prerequisites.name: Ordered hypergraph matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family of pairwise disjoint subsets of an ordered vertex set, with the induced order on each edge.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the family being counted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Interval-wise partite family
standard_prerequisites.statement: There are cut points splitting the order into consecutive blocks so that every edge meets each block in exactly the prescribed number of vertices.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structural hypothesis of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pattern parameters
standard_prerequisites.statement: To each pattern of signs compatible with the ordered partition the construction attaches a parameter, and the product of those parameters is the bound.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the factors of the asserted estimate.

core_obligations: Use the interval-wise structure to cut the order into blocks and map every edge to the tuple of its smallest vertex in each block, obtaining a set of distinct points in a real vector space (source lines 366-368).

For each sign pattern compatible with the ordered partition, bound the number of points whose coordinates grow and shrink according to that pattern by the corresponding parameter, using the monotonicity of the parameters and the fact that the quadrants are disjoint (source lines 370-373).
Apply the multidimensional Erdos-Szekeres theorem to cover all points by the finitely many quadrants and multiply the bounds to obtain the stated product (source lines 374-376).

proof_roadmap.step: Cut the order into blocks and encode each edge by its blockwise minima.
Bound each quadrant by its pattern parameter.
Cover by quadrants with the Erdos-Szekeres theorem and multiply.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 359-362: for a positive integer r, an ordered partition lambda of r and parameters attached to the patterns, any interval-wise lambda-partite family of edges has size at most the product of those parameters. The proof (source lines 365-377) is a covering argument whose three steps the statement does not show: the edges are encoded by the tuple of their smallest vertices in each block of the cutting of the order, so that pairwise disjointness makes those tuples distinct; the resulting point set is then split into the finitely many quadrants indexed by the sign patterns compatible with the ordered partition, and each quadrant is bounded by its own parameter, which is where the monotonicity of the parameters is used; finally the multidimensional Erdos-Szekeres theorem is invoked to see that every point lies in one of those quadrants. The statement records only the product bound.
